summary_plain: The Flame Extinguishment Experiment (FLEX) investigates the burning and extinction behavior of liquid fuel droplets, such as heptane and methanol, in the microgravity environment of the International Space Station. By burning these droplets in varying oxygen and inert-gas mixtures, researchers study how fires behave without the influence of buoyancy. These insights are vital for improving spacecraft fire safety and updating fire prevention standards for future missions.
summary_expert: FLEX utilized the Multi-user Droplet Combustion Apparatus (MDCA) within the Combustion Integrated Rack (CIR) on the ISS to perform 274 droplet combustion tests using heptane and methanol droplet fuels. Across these tests, ambient oxygen concentrations ranged from 12 to 34 percent, ambient pressures ranged from 70 to 309 kPa, and initial droplet diameters spanned 1.1 to 4.67 mm, utilizing diluents including N2, N2+CO2, and N2+He. Recorded outcomes across the flight test matrix included extinction in 186 tests, disruption in 61 tests, and completion in 27 tests, while burn times ranged from 0.3 to 39.2 s and flame extinction diameters ranged from 0 to 4.6 mm. The experiments identified both radiative and diffusive extinction limits, determined limiting oxygen indices (LOIs) lower than normal gravity predictions, and discovered stable, quasi-steady cool flames forming after the radiative extinction of visible flames in heptane droplets.

key_findings.text: FLEX ran 274 tests on the ISS, resulting in flame extinction in 186 tests, disruption in 61 tests, and completion in 27 tests.

The oxygen concentrations in FLEX tests ranged from 12 to 34 percent, with flames extinguishing in tests run at 12 to 30 percent oxygen and the lowest oxygen concentration burning to completion being 14 percent.
Initial droplet diameters ranged from 1.1 to 4.67 mm, burn times ranged from 0.3 to 39.2 s, and flame extinction diameters ranged from 0 to 4.6 mm.

The experiments identified radiative and diffusive extinction limits for heptane and methanol droplets, revealing a limiting oxygen index (LOI) significantly lower than in normal gravity and lower than previously predicted and anticipated.
FLEX observed stable, quasi-steady cool flames that form after the radiative extinction of the visible flame for heptane droplet combustion.

earth_applications: Improved fire safety in confined and reduced-gravity environments, such as submarines or high-altitude aircraft
Development of more efficient and less harmful fire suppression systems that reduce the risk of toxic byproducts during fire events
Informing the design of advanced combustion engines for improved fuel efficiency and reduced emissions in automotive and industrial applications
